findings.title: Local cache is populated before the limit check, so a rejected device bypasses the limit on its next request
findings.body: `tagDeviceUI` writes the device key into `localCache` (29‑minute TTL) *before* calling `anonStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice`. With this PR, `CreateOrUpdateDevice` can now fail with `ErrDeviceLimitReached`, and `Anonymous.Authenticate` turns that into an authentication failure. But because the cache entry was already set, every subsequent request from the same device within the next 29 minutes hits the cache early-return (`return nil`) in `tagDeviceUI`, `TagDevice` reports success, and `Authenticate` issues a normal anonymous identity. In practice the frontend fires many requests per page load, so at most the first one or two requests from an over-limit device get a 401 and the rest succeed — the configured `device_limit` is effectively not enforced. The cache must only be populated after the store call succeeds (and a rejection should not be cached, or should be cached as a negative result that keeps rejecting).

findings.title: Count-then-insert limit check is not atomic; concurrent new devices can exceed the limit
findings.body: `CreateOrUpdateDevice` runs `CountDevices` and then, if `count < deviceLimit`, performs an upsert in a separate session. Two or more first-time devices arriving concurrently (very likely with several Grafana replicas, since the per-instance `localCache` provides no cross-instance dedup) will all observe `count < limit` and all insert, so the stored device count can overshoot `device_limit`. If the limit is meant as a hard cap (e.g. for licensing/abuse control) this needs to be done in a single transaction with appropriate locking or a conditional insert; otherwise the setting should be documented as a soft limit. Additionally the `COUNT(*)` runs on every cache miss even when the device already exists and will simply be updated, which is an avoidable extra query on the request path.

findings.title: Device limit is only applied to requests carrying X-Grafana-Device-Id; omitting the header bypasses it entirely
findings.body: `TagDevice` returns `nil` immediately when the `X-Grafana-Device-Id` header is absent, and `Anonymous.Authenticate` then issues a full anonymous identity. The header is set voluntarily by the Grafana frontend JS; any client that strips it (curl, scripts, a modified browser) is never counted and never limited, so `auth.anonymous.device_limit` is trivially circumvented and cannot be relied on as an access control. If the limit is intended to be enforceable, requests without a device id should be rejected (or at least documented as uncounted) when a limit is configured.

findings.title: Limit tests only cover rejection of a new device; no coverage for existing-device updates or the service/client enforcement path
findings.body: `TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit` only asserts that a second, new device is rejected when `deviceLimit=1`. There is no test that an already-registered active device can still be updated once the limit is reached (the `updateDevice` success path and its `updated_at BETWEEN` window), no test that a stale device (older than 30 days) is treated as new, and no test at the `AnonDeviceService`/`Anonymous.Authenticate` level that a limit-exceeding device actually fails authentication on repeated requests. The last gap is exactly what hides the local-cache bypass bug in `tagDeviceUI`; a test issuing two `TagDevice`/`Authenticate` calls for the same over-limit device would have caught it.

findings.title: Limit-reached failure surfaces as a generic 401 and warning-level log noise
findings.body: `Authenticate` returns the raw `anonstore.ErrDeviceLimitReached` (a plain `fmt.Errorf`). The authn service joins it into the generic auth error, logs a `Warn` for every request, and middleware responds with a bare 401 'Unauthorized'; the frontend cannot distinguish 'device limit reached' from any other auth failure, so the newly exposed `anonymousDeviceLimit` setting cannot be used to show a meaningful message. The error is also logged at Debug in `TagDevice`, then re-logged upstream. Consider an `errutil` error with a public message/status so the UI can present the condition, and log at a lower level since this is expected behaviour under load.

findings.title: anonymousDeviceLimit is typed as `undefined` in the runtime config and the backend always sends a number
findings.body: `anonymousDeviceLimit = undefined;` with no type annotation gives the class property the literal type `undefined`, so `config.anonymousDeviceLimit` in `@grafana/runtime` is unusable for numeric comparisons without a cast (any `config.anonymousDeviceLimit > 0` is a compile error). Meanwhile `FrontendSettingsDTO.AnonymousDeviceLimit` is a non-omitempty `int64`, so the backend always serialises a number (0 when unset); the `number | undefined` type in `packages/grafana-data/src/types/config.ts` is therefore misleading as well. Declare it as `anonymousDeviceLimit = 0` (or `: number`) to match the wire format.

findings.title: New `device_limit` setting is not added to defaults.ini/sample.ini or configuration docs
findings.body: `cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit` is read from `[auth.anonymous] device_limit`, but the PR does not add the key to `conf/defaults.ini`, `conf/sample.ini`, or the configuration documentation, and the PR description leaves the why/who sections unfilled. Operators have no discoverable way to learn the setting exists, its default (0 = unlimited), or its semantics (30-day active-device window, soft limit, only applies to requests with a device id). Grafana convention is for every new ini key to appear in both ini files with a comment and in the configure-grafana docs.
